method: Read by hand in the release file (bootstrap.js: startup, launchBackendIfNeeded, provisionEnvironment, ensureVcRedistWindows, probeExistingUvBinary, resolveUvBinary, downloadStandaloneUv, PINNED_UV_HASHES; sidebar.js: the uv-missing card) and the README, compared line by line with the reviewed 0.92.1; the six pinned SHA-256 values checked against the .sha256 files Astral publishes with uv 0.13.8; every quote checked against the release file and README by script; level from the fixed rule; label and summary written by Claude Opus 5.5.
label: Downloads a fixed version of uv when it first sets up its Python
summary: The first time Zotero starts with it, it sets up its own Python: if it can't find uv on the computer, it downloads uv 0.13.8 from Astral's GitHub releases, and uv then installs Python 3.13. We checked that the fingerprints in the plugin match the ones Astral publishes for that version. Its README says it sets up Python with uv. On Windows, if Microsoft's C++ runtime is missing, it asks you to install it yourself rather than downloading it.

facts.what: uv 0.13.8, the Python package manager from Astral, as the release archive for the computer's system (macOS, Windows or Linux; Intel or ARM), unless a working uv is already on the computer (on the PATH, in the plugin's data folder, in ~/.local/bin or ~/.cargo/bin, or on Windows in the WinGet links folder or %USERPROFILE%\.local\bin); uv then installs Python 3.13 (Astral's own Python builds) into the plugin's data folder. Unlike 0.92.1, it no longer downloads Microsoft's Visual C++ runtime installer: on Windows, when vcruntime140_1.dll is missing, setup stops and the sidebar links to Microsoft's download page.
facts.readmeQuote: the extension automatically provisions an isolated, hermetic Python `3.13` runtime and `.venv` via [Astral `uv`](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv)
facts.notes: startup() (line 11) calls launchBackendIfNeeded() (line 298, defined at 2831), which provisions only when the plugin's .venv is missing (2913-2928). provisionEnvironment() (2386) first calls ensureVcRedistWindows() (2359): off Windows, or when vcruntime140_1.dll is present, it returns; otherwise it posts a notice and throws VCRUNTIME_MISSING with a link to learn.microsoft.com, and nothing is downloaded. resolveUvBinary() (2058) uses probeExistingUvBinary() (1957): a system uv, the plugin's own bin/uv, then the user locations, each passed through verifyUvBinary() (1642: at least 10 MB and an executable header). Only when none is usable does downloadStandaloneUv() (1765) run: it picks the target triple, takes the expected hash from PINNED_UV_HASHES (1662-1669; it throws if the triple has none), fetches the archive for PINNED_UV_VERSION over https (1776, 1784), rejects it under 1 MB, computes its SHA-256 (1791) and throws on a mismatch (1792) before writing it to disk (1798) and unpacking it; the unpacked binary is checked again by verifyUvBinary (1949). If the download fails, resolveUvBinary throws UV_MISSING with Astral's install command, and sidebar.js shows that command with a Copy button (2326 copies it to the clipboard); the plugin never runs it. 'uv python install 3.13' (2393) then fetches Python through uv. The plugin's own Python package is a wheel shipped in the .xpi; its install is the separate package-run finding. Someone upgrading with a .venv already in place doesn't provision again; one whose data folder still has a uv downloaded by 0.92.1 or earlier keeps using it if it passes verifyUvBinary.
facts.reviewerNote: Fingerprint written into the plugin and the program's maker, so CAP-DOWNLOAD-EXEC-FIXED (low). Checked on 2026-11-16 that all six values in PINNED_UV_HASHES equal the .sha256 files Astral publishes with uv 0.13.8 (github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/tag/0.13.8, a regular release of 2026-11-12). The scanner read the hash check as a checksum from the same place, but the hashes are a table in bootstrap.js; and it read the 'curl ... | sh' and 'irm ... | iex' strings as a shell download, but they are text the user may copy, never run. The README's Windows line still says setup 'automatically detects and installs' the C++ runtime; 0.93.1 doesn't, it asks you to install it. The reviewed 0.92.1 downloaded the latest uv and Microsoft's installer with no fingerprint (CAP-DOWNLOAD-EXEC-MAKER, low); this release changed both, so the old file is not listed in alsoAppliesTo.
